Date April 19, 1933

Subject (in full) Chan Yuen Sang (陈原生), member of the Communist Youth League -
subject of letter from H.B.M. Consulate-General dated 6/4/33.

Made by D.S.I. Everest. Forwarded by J.B. Ru. S.I.

In continuation of the attached report dated April 8,
1933, concerning a communist named Chan Yuen Sang (陈原生),
I have to state that further efforts made in co-operation
with the French Police and Chinese Authorities to ascertain
the whereabouts of this individual have been unsuccessful.
Particulars of Chan Yuen Sang have been added to our
list of suspects for future reference.

JR

D. S. I. Everest
D. S. I.

Special Branch S.B. Station
Date April 8, 1933.

Subject (in full) Chan Yuen Sang (陈原生), member of the Communist Youth League - subject of letter from H.B.M. Consulate General dated 6/4/33.

Made by D.S.I. Everest. Forwarded by J.B.R. S.I.

With reference to the attached letter dated April 6 from H.B.M. Consulate-General enclosing finger prints and photograph of a communist named Chan Yuen Sang (陈原生), who was arrested in Hongkong on December 14, 1932, and subsequently banished to Shanghai, I have to state that this person has not previously come to our notice and we have no knowledge of his whereabouts.

I respectfully suggest that a copy of the finger prints be obtained and filed with the Finger Print Bureau for future reference, and that six copies of the photograph of Chan Yuen Sang be made in order to facilitate further enquiries regarding this person in co-operation with the French Police and the Bureau of Public Safety.

D. S. I.
（签名：Everest）

事由（全称）陈原生（Chan Yuen Sang），共产主义青年团团员——系1933年4月6日英国驻上海总领事馆来函所涉人员。

由副督察长埃弗里斯特（Everest）拟写。由巡官 J.B.R. 转呈。

关于附上的4月6日英国驻上海总领事馆来信，信中附有一名名为陈原生（Chan Yuen Sang）的共产党员的指纹和照片，此人于1932年12月14日在香港被捕，随后被驱逐至上海，本人须陈述，此人此前未进入我方视线，我方亦不知其行踪。

谨建议获取一份指纹副本并存入指纹局以备日后查考，并制作六份陈原生照片副本，以便在与法租界巡捕房及公安局合作就此人进行进一步调查时使用。

C. & S. B. REGISTRY.

BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL,
P.O. BOX 257. SHANGHAI.
6th April, 1933.

My dear Givens,

I enclose herewith finger prints and photograph
from Shanghai
of one CHAN YUEN SANG who was sent down to Hongkong in
September 1932 as inspector of the Communist Youth Movement.
He was arrested in Hongkong on December 14th 1932 and after
his arrest made statements to the Police which proved of
great value to them with regard to the identity of certain
members of the Hongkong Communist Party. He was eventually
banished and despatched back to Shanghai where he presumably
still is. I should be interested to hear if you ever come
across him.

Yours sincerely,
[Signature]

(批：For record. [Signature] F.R.Simmons)

T.P.Givens, Esq.,
Special Branch,
S.M.P.

(批：S.B. 5/4.)

(批：S2,

report please. [Initials]

英国驻上海总领事馆，
上海邮政信箱257号。
1933年4月6日。

亲爱的吉文斯（Givens）：

现随函附上来自上海的一名陈原生（CHAN YUEN SANG）的指纹和照片，此人于1932年9月作为共产主义青年运动视察员被派往香港。他于1932年12月14日在香港被捕，被捕后向警方作了供述，这些供述对于查明香港共产党某些成员的身份极具价值。他最终被驱逐并遣返上海，据推测目前仍在上海。若你偶然发现此人，望告知，本人将不胜感激。

此致
敬礼，
[签名]

（批：存档。[签名] F.R.Simmons）

T.P.吉文斯（Givens）先生，
特别股，
上海公共租界工部局警务处。

（批：特别股 4月5日。）
